The riddle of the Sphinx is a classic enigma that has puzzled people for centuries. Here's the answer:

The riddle of the Sphinx is: "What is it that is blind, yet sees; silent, yet speaks; and is born, yet dies?"

Possible answers satisfying all conditions:

1. A river: A river is blind, yet it sees the world around it through its waters. It is silent, yet it speaks through its gentle flow. And it is born, yet dies, as it flows into the sea.
2. A tree: A tree is blind, yet it sees the world through its leaves. It is silent, yet it speaks through its bark. And it is born, yet dies, as it grows and dies seasonally.
3. A person: A person is blind, yet they see the world around them through their senses. They are silent, yet they speak through their words and actions. And they are born, yet die, as they grow and age.
4. A shadow: A shadow is blind, yet it sees the world around it through the light. It is silent, yet it speaks through the darkness. And it is born, yet dies, as it moves across the surface it follows.
5. A mirror: A mirror is blind, yet it sees the world around it through reflection. It is silent, yet it speaks through its surface. And it is born, yet dies, as it reflects the image of the world.

These are just a few possible answers that satisfy all the conditions of the riddle. There may be other answers as well.
